These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

Families after the 1900 burning

Burt Lake Band historian Alice Littlefield challenges the story that the burning of the village at Indian Point dispersed everyone elsewhere. Her 2005 essay describes families finding shelter with nearby relatives and rebuilding community life along Indian Road. She compares later accounts with land records, census material and recollections; those underlying records remain a further reading task.

Read the sources [1] Burt Lake Band

02

Food knowledge across generations

The Band’s Traditional Foods page describes collecting harvesting experiences, family stories and recipes that bring foods from the land into contemporary cooking. Its proposed book connects practical knowledge with family memory. The undated project account is a useful introduction to the community’s priorities; it does not establish the project’s present operation or outcomes.

Read the sources [2] Burt Lake Band

Community-published historical essayBurt Lake BandSource 1

What Happened After the Burnout? ↗

Publication: 2005-10-26

Tribal historian Alice Littlefield compares conflicting relocation stories and explains the evidence for continued community life near Indian Road. A useful correction to accounts of complete dispersal.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Both physical PDF pages 1-2 read as selectable text and rendered page images. Essay dated 26 October 2005; repost heading 31 January 2008. The cited research narrative, census originals, interviews and newspaper originals were not separately inspected. No legal acknowledgment conclusion adopted.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026

Community project accountBurt Lake BandSource 2

Traditional Foods ↗

The Band describes a food project linking harvesting knowledge, contemporary recipes and family recollections. It supplies a community perspective beyond the history of dispossession.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Entire two-paragraph public project body read. The page is undated and describes a three-year project; funding award, finished book, participation and present operation were not independently verified. Linked recipe book and photos not copied.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026
